name: Coulomb's law as the photon propagator
summary: The Green's function of Poisson's equation is the Fourier transform of the static one-photon-exchange propagator 1/q². In the Born approximation, tree-level exchange of a massless boson gives the 1/r potential and a massive one gives Yukawa's e^{-mr}/r.

name: Vacuum polarization: the vacuum as a dielectric
summary: Virtual e⁺e⁻ pairs screen a bare charge the way bound charges do in a dielectric, so the effective charge grows at short distances (the Uehling potential). The running α(Q²) behaves like a scale-dependent permittivity, rising from 1/137 to about 1/128 at m_Z.
breaks: Lorentz invariance forces εμ = 1 for the vacuum (there is no rest frame), the response depends on q² rather than on frequency alone, and the screening is UV-divergent. The bare charge cannot be observed, so it has to be renormalized.

name: Asymptotic freedom as vacuum paramagnetism
summary: Since εμ = 1 for a relativistic vacuum, antiscreening (ε < 1) is the same thing as paramagnetism (μ > 1). In the Nielsen–Hughes picture, the Pauli paramagnetism of spin-1 gluons outweighs their orbital Landau diamagnetism and quark screening, which gives the sign of the QCD β-function.
breaks: The picture is one-loop and perturbative. It says nothing directly about confinement, and the constant chromomagnetic background it uses is unstable (Nielsen–Olesen).

name: Magnetic spectrometry: momentum from track curvature
summary: Collider detectors measure momentum from how much charged tracks bend in solenoid or toroid fields (the 3.8 T CMS solenoid, the ATLAS toroids), designed from Biot–Savart field maps. Because the sagitta shrinks as 1/p, momentum resolution degrades in proportion to p.

name: MAC-E filter: adiabatic magnetic collimation (KATRIN)
summary: Tritium β electrons spiral along a field that falls by ~10⁴ from the source to the analysing plane. Adiabatic invariance of the magnetic moment converts transverse into longitudinal energy, so an electrostatic retarding potential becomes a sharp high-pass filter. KATRIN used this to set m_ν < 0.45 eV (90% CL, 2025).

name: 2D multipole expansion of accelerator magnets
summary: Accelerator magnet fields are written as a complex 2D multipole series: dipoles bend, quadrupoles focus, sextupoles correct chromaticity and octupoles damp instabilities. LHC magnet quality is specified by the error coefficients b_n and a_n, in units of 10⁻⁴ at R_ref = 17 mm.

name: Electric dipole moments as P- and T-odd multipoles
summary: A permanent EDM along a particle's spin is odd under both P and T, so by CPT it signals CP violation. Electron (ACME, JILA) and neutron EDM limits probe CP violation far beyond the tiny CKM-phase prediction and constrain baryogenesis models.
map: H=-\mu\,\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf B-d\,\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf E,\quad P,T:\ \boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf E\to-\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf E

name: E1/M1 radiative transitions in quarkonium
summary: Radiative decays such as ψ(2S)→γχ_cJ (E1) and J/ψ→γη_c (M1) obey the same multipole selection rules and rate formulas as atomic transitions. They were used to map the charmonium and bottomonium spectra and to test potential models.

name: Plasma frequency as photon mass: Anderson's route to Higgs
summary: Transverse waves in a plasma obey ω² = ω_p² + c²k², the dispersion relation of a massive photon. From plasmons and the Meissner effect, Anderson (1963) argued that gauge bosons can gain mass without a leftover Goldstone boson. Englert–Brout, Higgs and Guralnik–Hagen–Kibble made this precise, and it became electroweak symmetry breaking.
breaks: A plasma picks out a rest frame and breaks Lorentz invariance, and its longitudinal plasmon is not the W's longitudinal mode. The Higgs vacuum is Lorentz-invariant and has a physical scalar left over.

name: Euler–Heisenberg: the QED vacuum as a Kerr medium
summary: Integrating out the electron leaves four-photon operators suppressed by 1/m_e⁴, which act as a third-order susceptibility χ⁽³⁾ of the vacuum. This predicts light-by-light scattering, observed by ATLAS and CMS in ultraperipheral Pb–Pb collisions, and vacuum birefringence in strong fields, which has not yet been seen in the laboratory.

name: Strong-field QED at the laser intensity frontier
summary: Chirped-pulse amplification pushes laser fields toward the Schwinger critical field. Once the normalized amplitude a₀ ≫ 1, multiphoton processes stop being perturbative in the laser field, so nonlinear Compton scattering and multiphoton Breit–Wheeler pair creation (SLAC E144) are computed with laser-dressed Volkov propagators (Furry picture).

name: Cherenkov and transition-radiation particle ID
summary: RICH and DIRC detectors measure β from the Cherenkov angle, which together with the tracker momentum gives the mass and separates π, K and p (LHCb, ALICE, Belle II). Transition-radiation detectors such as the ATLAS TRT separate electrons from pions using the γ-dependence of transition-radiation yield.

name: Cherenkov light as the neutrino detector
summary: Water and ice detectors (Super-K, SNO, IceCube) see neutrino interactions through the Cherenkov cones of the charged secondaries. A sharp ring marks a muon and a fuzzy ring an electron shower, and the cone direction points back to the source. At EeV energies, coherent Askaryan radio emission from the shower's charge excess takes over (ARA, RNO-G).

name: Synchrotron loss sets collider size and choice of particle
summary: The relativistic Larmor (Liénard) power of a charge on a circular orbit grows as γ⁴/R², so the energy lost per turn limits circular e⁺e⁻ machines (the size of FCC-ee and CEPC). This pushes designs toward linear colliders or muons, which radiate (m_e/m_μ)⁴ ≈ 5×10⁻¹⁰ times less.

name: Angular ordering from coherent soft radiation
summary: In the QED Chudakov effect, a fresh e⁺e⁻ pair radiates soft photons mainly inside its opening angle, because outside it the pair looks neutral and the two amplitudes cancel. The same coherence orders successive gluon emissions in angle, which underlies angular-ordered parton showers and the hump-backed plateau of hadron spectra in jets.
breaks: Gluons carry colour and radiate themselves (C_A vs C_F). Colour-interference terms beyond leading N_c and non-global logarithms have no QED counterpart.

name: Bremsstrahlung, radiation length and EM showers
summary: High-energy electrons lose energy by bremsstrahlung (the QED version of radiation from a decelerated charge) and photons convert to pairs over 9X₀/7. Alternating these processes builds an electromagnetic shower whose depth grows like ln E, which is the basis of electromagnetic calorimetry.

name: Cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy (Project 8)
summary: Single β-decay electrons trapped in a magnetic field emit femtowatt cyclotron radiation, and its relativistic frequency gives their energy. Project 8 measured a first tritium spectrum and neutrino-mass limit this way (2023) and aims for ~40 meV sensitivity with atomic tritium.

name: Soft-photon theorem: classical radiation from sudden kicks
summary: The low-frequency Liénard–Wiechert spectrum of charges whose velocities change suddenly is exactly Weinberg's soft factor multiplying any QED amplitude. Its 1/ω photon number is the infrared divergence, which Bloch–Nordsieck summation over unresolved soft photons removes.

name: Classical self-energy and radiation reaction → mass renormalization
summary: A point electron's field energy diverges linearly as its radius goes to zero, and Abraham–Lorentz radiation reaction has runaway solutions. QED softens the divergence to a logarithm (Weisskopf 1939, through positron screening) and absorbs it into the observed mass — the first renormalization.

name: Coherent forward scattering → refractive index (MSW)
summary: A medium's refractive index is fixed by the forward scattering amplitude of its scatterers, the same physics as the optical theorem. Wolfenstein applied this to neutrinos: charged-current forward scattering on electrons gives ν_e an extra potential √2 G_F N_e, which changes the effective mixing in the Sun and Earth.
map: n-1=\frac{2\pi N f(0)}{k^2},\quad V_{CC}=\sqrt2\,G_FN_e,\quad \sigma_{\rm tot}=\frac{4\pi}{k}{\rm Im}f(0)

name: Thomson → Klein–Nishina: Compton scattering at tree level
summary: The classical Thomson cross-section 8πr_e²/3 is the ω→0 limit of the tree-level QED Klein–Nishina result. The low-energy theorem guarantees this limit holds to all orders, and Compton scattering was the first QED amplitude checked against experiment.

name: Random matrices and localization in the Dirac spectrum
summary: Low-lying eigenvalues of the QCD Dirac operator follow chiral random-matrix theory, and the Banks–Casher relation ties the chiral condensate to the spectral density at zero. Above T_c the low modes localize, with an Anderson-type mobility edge, linking chiral restoration to localization.
sources: Verbaarschot & Wettig (2000). "Random Matrix Theory and Chiral Symmetry in QCD". *Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 50, 343. [arXiv:hep-ph/0003017](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0003017)
Banks & Casher (1980). "Chiral symmetry breaking in confining theories". *Nucl. Phys. B* 169, 103. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(80)90255-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(80)90255-2)

name: Finite-temperature QFT: Matsubara formalism
summary: A thermal QFT is the Euclidean path integral on a spatial manifold times a circle of circumference ħβ, with bosons periodic and fermions antiperiodic. Matsubara frequencies ω_n=2πn/β or (2n+1)π/β turn the grand partition function into diagrammatic perturbation theory.
sources: Matsubara (1955). "A New Approach to Quantum-Statistical Mechanics". *Prog. Theor. Phys.* 14, 351. [doi:10.1143/PTP.14.351](https://doi.org/10.1143/PTP.14.351)

name: Entanglement entropy and the c-theorem
summary: In 1+1D CFT the entanglement entropy of an interval is (c/3) ln(ℓ/a), so the central charge is an entropy coefficient. Strong subadditivity of entanglement entropy gives an entropic proof that c decreases along RG flows.
sources: Calabrese & Cardy (2004). "Entanglement entropy and quantum field theory". *J. Stat. Mech.* P06002. [arXiv:hep-th/0405152](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405152)
Casini & Huerta (2004). "A finite entanglement entropy and the c-theorem". *Phys. Lett. B* 600, 142. [arXiv:hep-th/0405111](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405111)

name: Integrable field theory: Ising in a field and E8
summary: The 2D Ising critical point perturbed by a magnetic field is an integrable massive QFT with eight particles whose masses follow the E8 Lie algebra (m₂/m₁=2cos π/5, the golden ratio). Neutron scattering on the Ising-chain magnet CoNb₂O₆ observed the ratio.
sources: Coldea et al. (2010). "Quantum Criticality in an Ising Chain: Experimental Evidence for Emergent E8 Symmetry". *Science* 327, 177. [arXiv:1103.3694](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3694)

name: Exactly solvable lattice models as CFTs
summary: At criticality, exactly solved 2D models (Ising, Potts, vertex models, XXZ chain) are lattice realizations of conformal field theories. Their exponents are conformal weights, and finite-size spectra of transfer matrices give the central charge and scaling dimensions.
map: E_0(L)=Lf_\infty-\frac{\pi c v}{6L},\ E_n-E_0=\frac{2\pi v}{L}(h+\bar h)
sources: Belavin, Polyakov & Zamolodchikov (1984). "Infinite conformal symmetry in two-dimensional quantum field theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 241, 333. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X)

name: Directed percolation is Reggeon field theory
summary: The field theory of directed percolation is identical to Reggeon field theory, developed in the 1970s for high-energy hadron scattering. Its ε-expansion around d_c=4 transferred directly to absorbing-state transitions.
sources: Cardy & Sugar (1980). "Directed percolation and Reggeon field theory". *J. Phys. A* 13, L423. [doi:10.1088/0305-4470/13/12/002](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4470/13/12/002)
Hinrichsen (2000). "Non-equilibrium critical phenomena and phase transitions into absorbing states". *Adv. Phys.* 49, 815. [arXiv:cond-mat/0001070](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0001070)

name: Departure from equilibrium in baryogenesis
summary: Sakharov's third condition, departure from thermal equilibrium, is a statement of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics: in equilibrium CPT forces ⟨B⟩=0. Leptogenesis yields are computed from coupled Boltzmann equations for heavy-neutrino decays and washout.

name: WIMP freeze-out from the Boltzmann equation
summary: Relic dark-matter abundance comes from a Boltzmann equation in an expanding universe. Annihilation keeps n near equilibrium until the rate n⟨σv⟩ falls below H, after which the comoving density freezes out at Ω h²∝1/⟨σv⟩.
sources: Gondolo & Gelmini (1991). "Cosmic abundances of stable particles: improved analysis". *Nucl. Phys. B* 360, 145. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(91)90438-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(91)90438-4)
Bertone, Hooper & Silk (2005). "Particle dark matter: evidence, candidates and constraints". *Phys. Rep.* 405, 279. [arXiv:hep-ph/0404175](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0404175)

name: Quantum kinetic equations for dense neutrino gases
summary: In supernovae and the early universe, mixing neutrinos are described by a matrix-valued Boltzmann equation (flavour density matrices with collisions). Collective 'fast flavour' instabilities are analysed with linear-response stability theory, as for plasma waves.
sources: Sigl & Raffelt (1993). "General kinetic description of relativistic mixed neutrinos". *Nucl. Phys. B* 406, 423. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(93)90175-O](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(93)90175-O)
Fiorillo & Raffelt (2024). "Theory of neutrino fast flavor evolution. Part I. Linear response theory and stability conditions". *JHEP*. [arXiv:2406.06708](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06708)

name: Dispersion relations for hadronic vacuum polarization
summary: Causality and analyticity of the photon vacuum-polarization function give a Kramers–Kronig-type dispersion integral over σ(e⁺e⁻→hadrons). It is the data-driven route to the leading hadronic contribution to muon g−2, the same structure as the susceptibility relations of linear response.
sources: Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: Parton showers as Markov processes
summary: A parton shower is a Markov chain in an evolution variable. The Sudakov factor is the no-emission survival probability of a non-homogeneous Poisson process, and DGLAP evolution is a master equation for parton densities, so showers are sampled with veto algorithms from stochastic simulation.
sources: Sjöstrand et al. (2015). "An introduction to PYTHIA 8.2". *Comput. Phys. Commun.* 191, 159. [arXiv:1410.3012](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.3012)

name: Stochastic quantization and Hybrid Monte Carlo
summary: Parisi–Wu stochastic quantization obtains the Euclidean QFT measure e^{-S} as the equilibrium of Langevin dynamics in a fictitious time. Hybrid Monte Carlo, which combines molecular dynamics, momentum refreshment and a Metropolis test, is the workhorse algorithm of lattice QCD.

name: Euclidean QFT as statistical field theory
summary: Euclidean QFT in D dimensions is classical statistical mechanics of fields in D dimensions, with e^{-S_E/ħ} as Boltzmann weight. Particle-physics tools (Feynman diagrams, renormalization, instantons) and stat-mech tools (Monte Carlo, high-T expansions, RG) are interchangeable.

name: Critical points are conformal field theories
summary: At a continuous transition, scale invariance plus locality enhances to conformal invariance. The fixed point is a CFT whose operator dimensions are the critical exponents and whose OPE data fix all correlations.

name: Statistical field theory ↔ renormalizable QFT
summary: Landau–Ginzburg–Wilson field theory of a critical point is a Euclidean φ⁴ QFT. The correlation length plays the role of inverse mass, and the continuum limit at T_c is a renormalized massless QFT.

name: Electroweak crossover at T ~ 160 GeV
summary: Electroweak symmetry is restored at high temperature. Dimensional reduction to a 3D SU(2)-Higgs theory and lattice simulations show that for m_h=125 GeV the transition is a smooth crossover, beyond the endpoint (in the 3D Ising class) of the first-order line. Standard-Model electroweak baryogenesis is therefore ruled out.

name: Conformal bootstrap determinations of exponents
summary: Conformal bootstrap constraints (crossing symmetry plus unitarity) fix the 3D Ising, O(N) and other critical exponents to the highest precision available, ν≈0.62999 and η≈0.03630 for Ising, beyond Monte Carlo and the ε-expansion.
sources: El-Showk et al. (2012). "Solving the 3D Ising Model with the Conformal Bootstrap". *Phys. Rev. D* 86, 025022. [arXiv:1203.6064](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.6064)

name: Pisarski–Wilczek: universality of the chiral transition
summary: With symmetry and an ε-expansion, the QCD chiral transition with two massless flavours is in the 3D O(4) class, while with three massless flavours it must be first order (no infrared-stable fixed point). Physical quark masses turn it into a crossover at T_c≈156 MeV, with O(4) scaling still visible in lattice data.
map: SU(2)_L\times SU(2)_R\simeq O(4)\Rightarrow\text{3D }O(4)\ \text{class};\ N_f=3:\ \text{cubic invariant}\Rightarrow\text{first order}
sources: Pisarski & Wilczek (1984). "Remarks on the chiral phase transition in chromodynamics". *Phys. Rev. D* 29, 338. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.29.338](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.29.338)

name: 2D Ising as the c=1/2 minimal model
summary: The 2D Ising critical point is the M(4,3) minimal CFT with c=1/2. Its primaries σ (h=1/16) and ε (h=1/2) give η=1/4 and ν=1 exactly. In 3D the bootstrap places Ising at a kink on the boundary of allowed (Δ_σ, Δ_ε).
sources: Belavin, Polyakov & Zamolodchikov (1984). "Infinite conformal symmetry in two-dimensional quantum field theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 241, 333. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X)
El-Showk et al. (2012). "Solving the 3D Ising Model with the Conformal Bootstrap". *Phys. Rev. D* 86, 025022. [arXiv:1203.6064](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.6064)

name: Svetitsky–Yaffe: deconfinement in Z_N spin-model classes
summary: With the Polyakov loop as order parameter for center symmetry, a continuous deconfinement transition of a (d+1)-dimensional SU(N) gauge theory falls in the universality class of a d-dimensional Z_N spin model. Pure SU(2) in 3+1D deconfines in the 3D Ising class.
sources: Svetitsky & Yaffe (1982). "Critical behavior at finite-temperature confinement transitions". *Nucl. Phys. B* 210, 423. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(82)90172-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(82)90172-9)

name: Lattice gauge theory as statistical mechanics
summary: Wilson's lattice QCD is a statistical-mechanics model of group-valued link variables. Wegner's Z₂ lattice gauge theory is its Ising prototype with no local order parameter, strong-coupling expansions are high-temperature expansions, and Monte Carlo importance sampling carried over directly.
sources: Wilson (1974). "Confinement of quarks". *Phys. Rev. D* 10, 2445. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445)
Wegner (1971). "Duality in Generalized Ising Models and Phase Transitions without Local Order Parameters". *J. Math. Phys.* 12, 2259. [doi:10.1063/1.1665530](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1665530)
Creutz (1980). "Monte Carlo study of quantized SU(2) gauge theory". *Phys. Rev. D* 21, 2308. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.21.2308](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.21.2308)

name: Higgs potential as a Landau–Ginzburg free energy
summary: The Higgs potential has the Landau form with a sign-changing quadratic term. Its vacuum is spontaneously broken order, and coupling to gauge fields gives the Higgs–Anderson mechanism already known from Ginzburg–Landau superconductors.
sources: Englert & Brout (1964). "Broken Symmetry and the Mass of Gauge Vector Mesons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 321. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321)
Higgs (1964). "Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508)

name: NJL: BCS mean field for chiral symmetry breaking
summary: Nambu and Jona-Lasinio modelled nucleon mass generation explicitly on the BCS gap equation. The constituent mass is a self-consistent mean field from a four-fermion attraction, with pions as Goldstone modes, and the NJL model remains a mean-field tool for QCD phase diagrams.
sources: Nambu & Jona-Lasinio (1961). "Dynamical Model of Elementary Particles Based on an Analogy with Superconductivity. I". *Phys. Rev.* 122, 345. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.122.345](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.122.345)

name: Hierarchy problem as tuning to a critical point
summary: The Higgs mass term is the one relevant operator of the Standard Model. Keeping m_h ≪ Λ requires fine-tuning the bare parameter close to its critical value, just as a magnet must be tuned to T_c for ξ≫a. Naturalness asks what symmetry or dynamics does the tuning.
breaks: A magnet is tuned by an experimenter or by self-organized dynamics. For the Higgs no tuning agent is known (anthropics, SUSY, compositeness and relaxion proposals are all speculative), and the UV cutoff Λ may not exist physically.
sources: Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)

name: Wilsonian EFT: irrelevant operators and decoupling
summary: Effective field theory is the RG statement that operators of dimension above D are irrelevant, suppressed by (E/Λ)^{Δ-D}. Decoupling of heavy physics in particle physics and universality at critical points are the same fact.
sources: Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)
Weinberg (1979). "Phenomenological Lagrangians". *Physica A* 96, 327. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1)

name: Wilson's RG unifies running couplings and critical exponents
summary: QFT beta functions and the critical-phenomena RG are the same flow in theory space. A Wilson–Fisher fixed point is a zero of β(u), and the anomalous dimensions there are critical exponents, computed by the same diagrams in the ε-expansion.
sources: Wilson (1971). "Renormalization Group and Critical Phenomena. I. Renormalization Group and the Kadanoff Scaling Picture". *Phys. Rev. B* 4, 3174. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.4.3174](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.4.3174)
Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)

name: BKT, Coulomb gas and sine-Gordon duality
summary: The 2D XY vortex gas maps onto the 2D Coulomb gas and the sine-Gordon field theory, which Coleman showed is dual to the massive Thirring model. The Kosterlitz RG equations are the sine-Gordon beta functions, and β²=8π is the BKT point.
sources: Coleman (1975). "Quantum sine-Gordon equation as the massive Thirring model". *Phys. Rev. D* 11, 2088. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.11.2088](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.11.2088)

Kosterlitz & Thouless (1973). "Ordering, metastability and phase transitions in two-dimensional systems". *J. Phys. C* 6, 1181. [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/6/7/010)

name: Clocks search for ultralight dark matter
summary: Ultralight scalar dark matter would make fundamental constants oscillate; comparing clocks with different sensitivity to alpha and m_e/m_p detects such oscillations at frequencies set by the DM mass.
sources: Arvanitaki, Huang & Van Tilburg (2015). "Searching for dilaton dark matter with atomic clocks". *Phys. Rev. D* 91, 015015. [arXiv:1405.2925](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2925)

name: Isotope-shift King plots probe new bosons
summary: A new light boson coupling electrons to neutrons would bend the King plot of isotope shifts; precision ion spectroscopy constrains such Yukawa forces at keV-MeV masses.
sources: Berengut et al. (2018). "Probing New Long-Range Interactions by Isotope Shift Spectroscopy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 120, 091801. [arXiv:1704.05068](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.05068)

name: Electron g-2 and alpha test QED
summary: A single-electron Penning-trap measurement of g/2 and atom-recoil measurements of alpha (Cs, Rb) test QED at the 1e-13 level; their mutual tension is part of the lepton g-2 anomaly landscape.
sources: Fan et al. (2023). "Measurement of the Electron Magnetic Moment". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 130, 071801. [arXiv:2209.13084](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.13084)
Parker et al. (2018). "Measurement of the fine-structure constant as a test of the Standard Model". *Science* 360, 191. [arXiv:1812.04130](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.04130)

Morel et al. (2020). "Determination of the fine-structure constant with an accuracy of 81 parts per trillion". *Nature* 588, 61. [doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2964-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2964-7)

name: Lamb shift and the birth of renormalization
summary: The 1947 Lamb shift measurement and Bethe's mass-renormalized calculation launched renormalized QED; hydrogen spectroscopy remains a precision test of bound-state QED.
sources: Lamb & Retherford (1947). "Fine Structure of the Hydrogen Atom by a Microwave Method". *Phys. Rev.* 72, 241. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.72.241](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.72.241)
Bethe (1947). "The Electromagnetic Shift of Energy Levels". *Phys. Rev.* 72, 339. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.72.339](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.72.339)

name: Atomic parity violation measures the weak charge
summary: Z exchange between electrons and the nucleus mixes S and P states; the Cs 6S-7S parity-violating amplitude gives the nuclear weak charge and sin^2 theta_W at low momentum transfer, complementary to colliders.
sources: Wood et al. (1997). "Measurement of Parity Nonconservation and an Anapole Moment in Cesium". *Science* 275, 1759. [doi:10.1126/science.275.5307.1759](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.275.5307.1759)

name: Analog quantum simulation of lattice gauge theories
summary: Cold atoms and Rydberg arrays implement Hamiltonian lattice gauge theories with Gauss's law enforced by energy penalties or constraints, accessing real-time dynamics and finite density where Euclidean Monte Carlo has a sign problem.
sources: Bañuls et al. (2020). "Simulating lattice gauge theories within quantum technologies". *Eur. Phys. J. D* 74, 165. [arXiv:1911.00003](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00003)

name: Higgs amplitude mode in superfluids
summary: Near the superfluid-Mott transition, optical-lattice bosons have a gapped amplitude ('Higgs') mode of the order parameter, observed by lattice modulation spectroscopy.
breaks: No gauge field, so no Higgs mechanism; the amplitude mode can decay into Goldstone pairs and is only well defined near Lorentz-invariant criticality.
sources: Endres et al. (2012). "The 'Higgs' amplitude mode at the two-dimensional superfluid/Mott insulator transition". *Nature* 487, 454. [arXiv:1204.5183](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.5183)

name: Electron EDM in polar molecules
summary: Polar molecules (ThO, HfF+) amplify a lab field into internal effective fields of 10-100 GV/cm; spin-precession measurements bound the electron EDM below 1e-29 e cm, probing CP-violating physics at multi-TeV scales.
sources: ACME Collaboration (2018). "Improved limit on the electric dipole moment of the electron". *Nature* 562, 355. [doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0599-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0599-8)
Roussy et al. (2023). "An improved bound on the electron's electric dipole moment". *Science* 381, 46. [doi:10.1126/science.adg4084](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adg4084)

name: Leggett-Garg violation in neutrino oscillations
summary: Temporal (Leggett-Garg) inequalities, the time-domain analogue of Bell tests, are violated by MINOS oscillation data, showing neutrino flavour evolution is incompatible with macrorealism over 735 km.
sources: Formaggio et al. (2016). "Violation of the Leggett-Garg Inequality in Neutrino Oscillations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 117, 050402. [arXiv:1602.00041](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.00041)

name: Entangled neutral mesons and Bell tests
summary: Pairs of neutral K or B mesons from phi or Upsilon(4S) decays are produced in flavour-entangled EPR states, used to time-tag CP and flavour measurements and to test Bell-type inequalities with decaying systems.
breaks: Decay and lack of free measurement-setting choice prevent loophole-free Bell tests.
sources: Barr et al. (2024). "Quantum entanglement and Bell inequality violation at colliders". [arXiv:2402.07972](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07972)

name: Wave-packet decoherence of neutrino oscillations
summary: Mass eigenstates in a neutrino wave packet separate over a coherence length, damping oscillations exactly as which-path information kills interference; open-system (Lindblad) models also bound exotic decoherence from new physics.
sources: Akhmedov & Smirnov (2009). "Paradoxes of neutrino oscillations". *Phys. Atom. Nucl.* 72, 1363. [arXiv:0905.1903](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.1903)

name: Kaon mixing is a non-Hermitian two-level system
summary: The Weisskopf-Wigner effective Hamiltonian of neutral kaons (or B mesons) is the non-Hermitian matrix M - i Gamma/2; its non-orthogonal eigenstates K_S, K_L and their overlap encode CP violation.
sources: Lee, Oehme & Yang (1957). "Remarks on Possible Noninvariance under Time Reversal and Charge Conjugation". *Phys. Rev.* 106, 340. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.106.340](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.106.340)

name: Entanglement of top-quark pairs at the LHC
summary: Top-antitop spin correlations reconstructed from decay leptons are a two-qubit density matrix; ATLAS and CMS observed entanglement near threshold using quantum-information witnesses.
sources: ATLAS Collaboration (2024). "Observation of quantum entanglement with top quarks at the ATLAS detector". *Nature* 633, 542. [arXiv:2311.07288](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07288)
Barr et al. (2024). "Quantum entanglement and Bell inequality violation at colliders". [arXiv:2402.07972](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07972)

name: Entanglement entropy measures the central charge
summary: In a 1+1D CFT the entanglement entropy of an interval grows logarithmically with a coefficient fixed by the central charge, so entanglement diagnoses criticality and universality classes.
sources: Calabrese & Cardy (2004). "Entanglement entropy and quantum field theory". *J. Stat. Mech.* 0406, P06002. [arXiv:hep-th/0405152](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405152)
Holzhey, Larsen & Wilczek (1994). "Geometric and renormalized entropy in conformal field theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 424, 443. [arXiv:hep-th/9403108](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9403108)

name: Quantum machine learning for collider data
summary: Variational quantum classifiers and kernels have been tried on jet tagging and event classification; no advantage over classical deep learning has been demonstrated.
sources: Biamonte et al. (2017). "Quantum machine learning". *Nature* 549, 195. [arXiv:1611.09347](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.09347)

name: Quantum algorithms for parton showers
summary: Quantum circuits can simulate parton showers including quantum interference between emission histories that classical Markov showers drop.
sources: Bauer et al. (2021). "Quantum Algorithm for High Energy Physics Simulations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 126, 062001. [arXiv:1904.03196](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.03196)

name: Digital quantum algorithms for QFT
summary: Hamiltonian-simulation algorithms compute scattering in scalar and gauge field theories in polynomial time, a route around the sign problem of lattice QCD at finite density and real time.
sources: Jordan, Lee & Preskill (2012). "Quantum Algorithms for Quantum Field Theories". *Science* 336, 1130. [arXiv:1111.3633](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.3633)

name: Qubit photon counting for dark-photon searches
summary: A transmon dispersively coupled to a cavity counts photons by repeated quantum non-demolition parity measurements, evading the standard quantum limit of linear amplifiers in hidden-photon and axion searches.
sources: Dixit et al. (2021). "Searching for Dark Matter with a Superconducting Qubit". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 126, 141302. [arXiv:2008.12231](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.12231)

name: Trapped-ion simulation of the Schwinger model
summary: A few trapped-ion qubits simulated real-time pair creation in 1+1D QED after eliminating the gauge field; circuit-QED and tensor-network studies extend this to meson scattering.
sources: Martinez et al. (2016). "Real-time dynamics of lattice gauge theories with a few-qubit quantum computer". *Nature* 534, 516. [arXiv:1605.04570](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.04570)
Belyansky et al. (2024). "High-Energy Collision of Quarks and Mesons in the Schwinger Model: From Tensor Networks to Circuit QED". [arXiv:2307.02522](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.02522)

name: Second quantization: QM of many particles is QFT
summary: Non-relativistic many-body quantum mechanics in Fock space is a free or interacting quantum field theory; relativistic QFT adds Lorentz invariance, antiparticles and particle number non-conservation.

name: Neutrino flavour as a precessing pseudo-spin
summary: Two-flavour oscillation is spin-1/2 precession in an effective magnetic field; the oscillation formula is the Rabi formula, and collective oscillations in dense neutrino gases map onto interacting spin models.

name: Isospin and flavour multiplets via SU(2) recoupling
summary: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and the Wigner-Eckart theorem developed for angular momentum organize isospin and flavour multiplets, decay branching ratios and helicity amplitudes of hadrons.

name: MSW conversion as an adiabatic level crossing
summary: Resonant flavour conversion in the Sun is an avoided crossing of matter-dressed mass eigenstates; adiabatic following gives near-complete conversion and the non-adiabatic hopping probability is the Landau-Zener formula.
sources: Parke (1986). "Nonadiabatic Level Crossing in Resonant Neutrino Oscillations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 57, 1275. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.1275](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.1275)
Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)

name: Schrieffer-Wolff elimination as integrating out
summary: Adiabatic elimination of high-energy states by second-order perturbation theory (Schrieffer-Wolff) gives effective Hamiltonians, the same logic as integrating out heavy fields; Fermi's four-fermion coupling is W exchange at second order.

name: Golden rule and decay widths
summary: Fermi's golden rule is the non-relativistic form of the relativistic decay-rate and cross-section formulas built from Feynman amplitudes and Lorentz-invariant phase space.

name: Supersymmetric quantum mechanics
summary: Witten introduced SUSY QM as a toy model of supersymmetry breaking (Witten index); it became a tool for exactly solvable potentials through shape invariance and partner Hamiltonians.
sources: Witten (1981). "Dynamical breaking of supersymmetry". *Nucl. Phys. B* 188, 513. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(81)90006-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(81)90006-7)
Cooper, Khare & Sukhatme (1995). "Supersymmetry and quantum mechanics". *Phys. Rep.* 251, 267. [arXiv:hep-th/9405029](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9405029)

name: Quarkonium as hydrogen of QCD
summary: Charmonium and bottomonium spectra follow from a Schrodinger equation with a Coulomb-plus-linear (Cornell) potential, organized like hydrogen and positronium levels with fine and hyperfine splittings.
breaks: Confinement (linear term) has no atomic analogue; relativistic corrections and coupled open-flavour channels matter above threshold.
sources: Eichten et al. (1975). "Spectrum of Charmed Quark-Antiquark Bound States". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 34, 369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.369)

name: Theta vacua as Bloch states; WZ terms as Berry phases
summary: Large gauge transformations make the Yang-Mills vacuum periodic, and theta plays the role of Bloch quasi-momentum in a periodic potential; Wess-Zumino-Witten terms are Berry phases of the low-energy fields.
sources: Jackiw & Rebbi (1976). "Vacuum Periodicity in a Yang-Mills Quantum Theory". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 37, 172. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.172](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.172)

name: Wilson loops are non-abelian holonomies
summary: The Aharonov-Bohm phase is a U(1) holonomy; Yang-Mills Wilson loops are its non-abelian generalization, and degenerate adiabatic transport produces the same Wilczek-Zee non-abelian connection.
sources: Aharonov & Bohm (1959). "Significance of Electromagnetic Potentials in the Quantum Theory". *Phys. Rev.* 115, 485. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.115.485](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.115.485)
Wu & Yang (1975). "Concept of nonintegrable phase factors and global formulation of gauge fields". *Phys. Rev. D* 12, 3845. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.12.3845](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.12.3845)
Wilczek & Zee (1984). "Appearance of Gauge Structure in Simple Dynamical Systems". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 52, 2111. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111)

name: Instantons from double wells to QCD
summary: Euclidean instantons that compute tunnelling splitting in a double well become Yang-Mills instantons, which break U(1)_A through the anomaly and mix the theta vacua.
sources: 't Hooft (1976). "Symmetry Breaking through Bell-Jackiw Anomalies". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 37, 8. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.8](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.37.8)

name: Feynman path integral from particles to fields
summary: The QFT generating functional is the particle path integral with paths replaced by field configurations; stationary phase gives the classical field equations and Gaussian integrals give propagators and Wick's theorem.
sources: Feynman (1948). "Space-Time Approach to Non-Relativistic Quantum Mechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 20, 367. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.20.367)

name: Born series as tree-level perturbation theory
summary: The Lippmann-Schwinger Born series is the non-relativistic limit of the Feynman-diagram expansion: first Born approximation equals tree-level one-boson exchange (Yukawa/Coulomb), and the optical theorem is S-matrix unitarity.
map: f_{\rm Born}=-\frac{m}{2\pi\hbar^2}\tilde V(\mathbf q)\leftrightarrow\mathcal M\propto\frac{g^2}{q^2+m^2};\ \sigma_{\rm tot}=\frac{4\pi}{k}\mathrm{Im}f(0)

name: Near-threshold states and universality
summary: Hadrons near a two-body threshold (deuteron, X(3872)) are governed by a large scattering length, the same universal physics as Feshbach-tuned cold atoms, including Efimov-type three-body effects.
sources: Braaten & Hammer (2006). "Universality in few-body systems with large scattering length". *Phys. Rep.* 428, 259. [arXiv:cond-mat/0410417](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0410417)

name: Quantized EM field as free QFT
summary: Quantum optics' mode expansion of the field, Fock and coherent states are the canonical quantization of free Maxwell theory; Glauber coherent states are the quantum states closest to classical fields.
sources: Glauber (1963). "The Quantum Theory of Optical Coherence". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 2529. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.2529)

name: Single-photon detectors in particle detectors
summary: Calorimeters, Cherenkov and scintillator systems read out light with single-photon-sensitive devices (PMTs, SiPMs, SPAD arrays); quantum-optics detector metrics such as efficiency, dark counts and timing jitter set detector performance.

name: Squeezed-state receivers for axion haloscopes
summary: Haloscopes convert axions to microwave photons in a resonant cavity; HAYSTAC injected squeezed vacuum to beat the quantum limit on scan rate, a direct import of quantum metrology.
sources: Backes et al. (2021). "A quantum enhanced search for dark matter axions". *Nature* 590, 238. [arXiv:2008.01853](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01853)

name: Primordial black holes as dark matter
summary: PBHs are a non-particle dark-matter candidate; Hawking evaporation removes those below about 5e14 g and gamma-ray and CMB limits constrain slightly heavier ones, while lensing and GW limits leave the asteroid-mass window open.
sources: Carr et al. (2021). "Constraints on primordial black holes". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 84, 116902. [arXiv:2002.12778](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.12778)

name: Black-hole superradiance probes ultralight bosons
summary: A boson whose Compton wavelength matches a Kerr black hole forms hydrogen-like bound states that grow by superradiance while omega < m Omega_H, spinning the hole down; measured BH spins and continuous GW searches exclude axion masses near 1e-13 to 1e-11 eV.
sources: Arvanitaki & Dubovsky (2011). "Exploring the String Axiverse with Precision Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. D* 83, 044026. [arXiv:1004.3558](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.3558)
Arvanitaki et al. (2010). "String Axiverse". *Phys. Rev. D* 81, 123530. [arXiv:0905.4720](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.4720)

name: The cosmological constant problem
summary: Lorentz invariance forces vacuum energy to enter the Einstein equations as rho_vac g_munu, so QFT zero-point energy, the Higgs potential and the QCD condensate all contribute to Lambda; naive estimates exceed the observed (2.2 meV)^4 by 50-120 orders of magnitude.
map: \langle T_{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\rm vac}=-\rho_{\rm vac}g_{\mu\nu}\Rightarrow\Lambda_{\rm eff}=\Lambda+8\pi G\rho_{\rm vac}/c^4,\ \rho_{\rm obs}\approx(2.2\,\text{meV})^4
sources: Weinberg (1989). "The Cosmological Constant Problem". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 61, 1. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1)

name: Gravity as a gauge theory of the Lorentz group
summary: Gauging local Lorentz (Poincare) invariance gives the spin connection as gauge potential and the Riemann tensor as its field strength, so GR in tetrad form shares the fibre-bundle structure of Yang-Mills.
sources: Utiyama (1956). "Invariant theoretical interpretation of interaction". *Phys. Rev.* 101, 1597. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.101.1597](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.101.1597)
Kibble (1961). "Lorentz invariance and the gravitational field". *J. Math. Phys.* 2, 212. [doi:10.1063/1.1703702](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1703702)

name: Higgs inflation is a scalar-tensor theory
summary: A large non-minimal coupling xi h^2 R makes the SM Higgs the inflaton; transforming to the Einstein frame flattens the potential into the same plateau as Starobinsky R+R^2 gravity, giving n_s near 0.965 and r near 0.003.
sources: Bezrukov & Shaposhnikov (2008). "The Standard Model Higgs boson as the inflaton". *Phys. Lett. B* 659, 703. [arXiv:0710.3755](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.3755)

name: Sub-millimetre tests of the inverse-square law
summary: ADD extra dimensions turn Newtonian gravity into a steeper power law below the compactification radius, parametrized as a Yukawa correction; torsion-balance tests of Newton's law below 0.1 mm bound n=2 ADD radii to tens of micrometres.
sources: Kapner et al. (2007). "Tests of the Gravitational Inverse-Square Law below the Dark-Energy Length Scale". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 98, 021101. [arXiv:hep-ph/0611184](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0611184)

name: Worldline EFT (NRGR) for compact binaries
summary: Non-relativistic GR treats compact bodies as point particles on worldlines with finite-size operators (tidal Love numbers) and integrates out potential and radiation gravitons with Feynman diagrams and dimensional regularization, the EFT toolkit of QCD applied to post-Newtonian inspirals.
map: S=-m\int d\tau+c_E\int d\tau\,E_{\mu\nu}E^{\mu\nu}+\dots,\quad v^2\sim Gm/r\ \text{as expansion parameter}
sources: Goldberger & Rothstein (2006). "An effective field theory of gravity for extended objects". *Phys. Rev. D* 73, 104029. [arXiv:hep-th/0409156](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0409156)

name: Amplitudes compute post-Minkowskian binary dynamics
summary: On-shell scattering amplitudes, unitarity cuts and the eikonal give the conservative two-body Hamiltonian order by order in G (post-Minkowskian), now at 3PM-5PM, feeding EOB waveform models for LIGO and LISA.
breaks: Amplitudes give scattering (unbound) orbits most naturally; bound-orbit observables need analytic continuation (B2B maps) and radiation-reaction subtleties remain.
sources: Bern et al. (2019). "Scattering Amplitudes and the Conservative Hamiltonian for Binary Systems at Third Post-Minkowskian Order". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 122, 201603. [arXiv:1901.04424](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.04424)

name: Nanohertz GWs from axion domain walls
summary: Collapsing domain walls of QCD-coupled axions, cosmic strings and QCD-scale phase transitions all produce stochastic GW backgrounds peaking near nanohertz; PTA spectra are fitted against these alongside supermassive-binary models.
breaks: The supermassive-black-hole-binary interpretation remains adequate; cosmological fits are not preferred decisively.
sources: Kitajima et al. (2024). "Gravitational waves from domain wall collapse, and application to nanohertz signals with QCD-coupled axions". *Phys. Lett. B* 851, 138586. [arXiv:2306.17146](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.17146)
NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Search for Signals from New Physics". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L11. [arXiv:2306.16219](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16219)

name: Cosmic strings from GUT symmetry breaking
summary: U(1) factors broken in GUT chains leave cosmic strings (possibly metastable via monopole nucleation) whose loops radiate a broad GW background; PTA amplitudes bound the string tension G mu, constraining breaking scales.
sources: NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Search for Signals from New Physics". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L11. [arXiv:2306.16219](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16219)
Caprini & Figueroa (2018). "Cosmological backgrounds of gravitational waves". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 35, 163001. [arXiv:1801.04268](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04268)

name: LISA tests first-order electroweak transitions
summary: Electroweak baryogenesis needs a strongly first-order transition; bubble collisions, sound waves and turbulence in that transition produce a GW background peaking near millihertz, squarely in the LISA band.
sources: LISA Cosmology Working Group (2024). "Gravitational waves from first-order phase transitions in LISA: reconstruction pipeline and physics interpretation". *JCAP* 10, 020. [arXiv:2403.03723](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03723)
Caprini & Figueroa (2018). "Cosmological backgrounds of gravitational waves". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 35, 163001. [arXiv:1801.04268](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04268)

name: Graviton as a spin-2 quantum field
summary: Perturbative quantum gravity is QFT applied to the metric: expand g=eta+kappa h, quantize the massless spin-2 field with gauge fixing and ghosts as in Yang-Mills; the coupling kappa^2=32 pi G has mass dimension -2, so the theory is non-renormalizable and needs a UV completion.
sources: Burgess (2004). "Quantum gravity in everyday life: General relativity as an effective field theory". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 7, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0311082](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0311082)
Donoghue (1994). "General relativity as an effective field theory: The leading quantum corrections". *Phys. Rev. D* 50, 3874. [arXiv:gr-qc/9405057](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9405057)

name: GR as an effective field theory
summary: Power counting in E/M_Pl makes GR a predictive EFT: the Einstein-Hilbert term is leading, R^2 terms are suppressed, and the long-distance quantum correction to the Newtonian potential is computable and cutoff-independent, exactly like chiral perturbation theory.
sources: Burgess (2004). "Quantum gravity in everyday life: General relativity as an effective field theory". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 7, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0311082](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0311082)
Donoghue (1994). "General relativity as an effective field theory: The leading quantum corrections". *Phys. Rev. D* 50, 3874. [arXiv:gr-qc/9405057](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9405057)

name: Double copy: gravity = (gauge theory)^2
summary: Tree and loop gravity amplitudes are obtained from Yang-Mills amplitudes by replacing colour factors with kinematic numerators that obey the same Jacobi identities (BCJ), generalizing the KLT relations of string theory; the classical double copy maps Coulomb to Schwarzschild.
map: \mathcal A^{\rm YM}=\sum_i\frac{c_in_i}{D_i}\ \to\ \mathcal M^{\rm grav}=\sum_i\frac{n_i\tilde n_i}{D_i},\quad c_i\to n_i,\ g\to\kappa/2
sources: Bern, Carrasco & Johansson (2010). "Perturbative Quantum Gravity as a Double Copy of Gauge Theory". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 105, 061602. [arXiv:1004.0476](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.0476)

name: AdS/CFT: bulk gravity equals boundary CFT
summary: Type IIB string theory on AdS5xS5 is conjectured to be exactly N=4 SU(N) super-Yang-Mills; the GKP-Witten dictionary maps bulk fields of mass m to CFT operators of dimension Delta, and the bulk on-shell action to the CFT generating functional.
sources: Maldacena (1998). "The Large N Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 231. [arXiv:hep-th/9711200](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9711200)
Witten (1998). "Anti de Sitter space and holography". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 253. [arXiv:hep-th/9802150](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9802150)
Gubser, Klebanov & Polyakov (1998). "Gauge theory correlators from noncritical string theory". *Phys. Lett. B* 428, 105. [arXiv:hep-th/9802109](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9802109)

name: Wilson loops as minimal string worldsheets
summary: In AdS/CFT the expectation value of a Yang-Mills Wilson loop is the exponential of minus the regularized area of a string worldsheet ending on the loop, giving the strong-coupling quark-antiquark potential V proportional to -sqrt(lambda)/L.
sources: Maldacena (1998). "Wilson loops in large N field theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 4859. [arXiv:hep-th/9803002](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9803002)
